2607.21131.title: Demographically-Informed Heat-Mortality Risk Curves via Risk Graph Neural Networks
2607.21131.paper_summary: Estimating heat-related mortality risk is a core task in environmental epidemiology, typically addressed with Distributed Lag Non-linear Models (DLNMs); interpretable exposure-response surfaces fitted to temperature-mortality time series. DLNMs are effective but ignore demographic and geographic context, despite well-established relevance to heat vulnerability. We propose Risk Graph Neural Networks (RGNNs), a hierarchical GNN encoder that uses granular census features to optimise DLNM coefficient vectors, preserving interpretable risk curve outputs while substantially improving predictive calibration. Evaluated across 10 regions of England and Wales on two unprecedented heat years, RGNN variants maintain both lower point-errors and near-nominal uncertainty coverage during the 2022 heatwave where baselines collapse.
2607.21131.paper_summary_zh: 估算與熱相關的死亡風險是環境流行病學中的核心任務，通常使用分佈滯後非線性模型（DLNMs）來處理；這些模型為溫度-死亡時間序列擬合可解釋的暴露-反應曲面。DLNMs 是有效的，但忽略了人口和地理背景，儘管這對熱脆弱性有著良好的相關性。我們提出了風險圖神經網絡（RGNNs），這是一種層次化的 GNN 編碼器，利用細粒度的人口普查特徵來優化 DLNM 係數向量，保留可解釋的風險曲線輸出，同時顯著改善預測校準。在英格蘭和威爾士的 10 個地區對兩個前所未有的熱年進行評估，RGNN 變體在 2022 年熱浪期間保持了較低的點誤差和接近名義的不確定性覆蓋，當時基準崩潰。
